Connecting Plato
Questions? Reply to your 41 Labs contact.

Connecting your Plato account

At the end of this guide, your AI shows real free times from Plato and books patients in the way you choose.

The API key is made in Plato under System Setup → General Settings → API. If you cannot see that screen, ask whoever manages your Plato account.

If you saw Plato is connected, but your choices did not save before, open Settings → Connections → Plato and connect again. Nothing is lost. The steps are under Replace your API key at the end of this guide.

Before you start

You need:

  • A Plato login that can open System Setup.
  • Your dashboard, with the owner or admin role.
  • Your opening hours, lunch break and the dates you are closed.
  • A phone for the test in Steps 12 and 13. Its number is not on your alert list (Settings → Team & Alerts) and not in Plato.
  • About 20 minutes.

What we ask you for

Clinic account in PlatoPlato's name for your clinic. It is the word after /api/ in your Plato address. Plato support can confirm it.
API keyIn Plato: System Setup → General Settings → API, then Generate API Key. Treat it like a password.

What happens in this guide

Step 1 is in Plato. Step 2 is on Settings → Connections. Steps 3 to 11 are on one screen, Connect Plato, in four parts: Test the key, Name calendars, Opening hours and Who books. Steps 12 and 13 are the test on your phone. Step 14 is a switch you make after your first week.

The six stages of connecting Plato, with the steps each one covers.

Step by step

01

Make an API key in Plato

  1. In Plato, open System Setup → General Settings.
  2. Open the API tab.
  3. Press Generate API Key.
  4. Copy the key.

Send the key to nobody. Paste it into your dashboard only.

Screenshot to come: the Plato screen System Setup → General Settings → API, with the Generate API Key button.

02

Open Plato on the Connections screen

  1. In your dashboard, go to Settings → Connections.
  2. Press the Booking chip.
  3. Under Add more, find Plato.
  4. Press Connect.
03

Enter your clinic account and key

The Connect Plato screen opens on part 1 of 4, Test the key.

  1. Type your clinic account in Clinic account in Plato.
  2. Paste the key into API key.
  3. Press Test the connection.

The test saves nothing.

04

Check the free times are yours

A green box reads Plato answered, with the number of calendars and up to three free times.

What to do after Test the connection, for each of the three results.

  1. Open your Plato diary for the day shown.
  2. Check that each time is free in Plato.
  3. Press Name the calendars.

Screenshot to come: your Plato diary for the day shown, with the free times to check.

05

Name the calendars your patients know

Part 2 of 4, Name calendars, lists every calendar in Plato. Each box starts with the name from Plato.

  1. Change a name to the one your patients use, such as the therapist or the room.
  2. Switch off any calendar your AI must never book.
  3. Check the badge counts the calendars your AI may book.
  4. Press Next: set opening hours.

Next stays off until at least one calendar is switched on.

06

Check your opening hours

Part 3 of 4, Opening hours, shows a week. It starts with Monday to Friday 09:00 to 18:00, Saturday 09:00 to 13:00 and Sunday closed, or with the hours you saved before. Each Last start box reads Not set until you type a time.

  1. For each day, set the opening and the closing time.
  2. Switch off a day you are closed.
  3. Under Each appointment, pick 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120 minutes.
07

Set a last start and a lunch break

Both are optional. With Last start on Not set, an appointment only has to end by closing time.

  1. Click a Last start box and type a time.
  2. Switch on Lunch for a day and set its start and end.

You will see no time after the last start, and no time over the lunch break:

A day with lunch, a last start and 2 hours of notice: the green times are offered.

08

Set the booking limits

  1. Under Earliest new booking, pick 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, 24, 48 or 72 hours.
  2. Under Furthest booking, pick 7, 14, 30, 60, 90 or 180 days.
  3. Under Closed dates, pick a date and press Add date for each day off.
  4. Press Next: choose who books.

The defaults are 1 hour and 30 days. You can list up to 60 closed dates.

Furthest booking 30 days and two closed dates: the green days are offered.

09

Choose who books

Part 4 of 4, Who books.

  1. Pick one of the three choices. For your first week, pick Your AI books, your team confirms.

It is the choice selected when you first open this part. What you will see for each choice:

The three Who books choices, row by row.

10

Choose when a person steps in

Under Hand to a person when, your AI stops and alerts your team on WhatsApp, whatever you picked under Who books.

  1. For your first week, switch on The patient is new.
  2. Under A change or cancel comes in late, pick 12, 24 or 48 hours.

The patient is new means the WhatsApp number is not in Plato yet. It is off until you switch it on. With it on, your team creates the patient record and books. A change or cancel comes in late is on by default, at 24 hours.

A hand-over, from your AI's last message to your team's answer.

11

Save the connection

  1. Press Connect Plato.

The key and every choice from Steps 5 to 10 are saved together.

A red banner above the buttons means nothing was saved. Fix what the banner names, and press Connect Plato again.

When the save works, the Plato page opens with the green Working pill and Connected as followed by your clinic account.

On Settings → Connections, the Plato card now sits under Connected.

12

Pick a phone that is not on your alert list

Your alert list is on Settings → Team & Alerts. Your AI does not answer a number on it, so test from a phone that is not there. The number must not be in Plato either.

Which phone to test from.

13

Test it from that phone

  1. From the test phone, message your business WhatsApp number and ask for an appointment.
  2. Pick one of the times your AI offers.
  3. Read your AI's answer. With The patient is new on, it says your team will confirm the time and books nothing.
  4. Check your team's WhatsApp for one alert about this booking.
  5. Open your Inbox. The chat shows under Needs your input, with a card.
  6. Book the time in Plato yourself, then press Mark as read on the card.

What you will see in the chat:

A new patient with The patient is new on: your AI books nothing and says your team will confirm.

Screenshot to come: the WhatsApp alert your team gets, with the name and the time.

If you left The patient is new off, your AI asks for a full name, adds the patient with name and phone only, and books. The appointment shows in Plato as Scheduled until your team confirms it. The full test, with a move, a cancel and every hand-over, is in Connecting your Plato booking rules at docs.41labs.ai/hermes/plato-how-booking-works.

14

Switch to Your AI books it after your first week

  1. After your first week, open Settings → Connections → Plato.
  2. Under Who books, pick Your AI books it.
  3. Under Hand to a person when, leave The patient is new on, or switch it off.

Each change saves at once. What changes:

The setting for your first week, and the setting you switch to after it.

Checklist

Replace your API key

Use these steps to replace a key, or to connect again after you saw Plato is connected, but your choices did not save. Make a new key in Plato first (Step 1) if you no longer have the key. From the moment you press Disconnect Plato, your AI hands every booking to your team until you connect again.

Replacing your API key, from the Plato page to Working.

  1. Open Settings → Connections → Plato.
  2. Press Disconnect Plato at the bottom of the page, then press Disconnect Plato in the box.
  3. On Settings → Connections, find Plato under Add more and press Connect.
  4. Type the same clinic account, paste the key, and press Test the connection.
  5. Go through the four parts. Your names, hours, limits and choices are already filled in.
  6. Press Connect Plato.

When the page shows Needs you, press Connect again and skip the first two steps.

If something goes wrong

At Step 3 or 4, a red line under API key:

The Plato account name has only letters, digits, _ or -. It is the word after /api/ in your Plato address. Ask your Plato admin if you are not sure.Type the account name without spaces or other characters.
Plato did not accept this key. Check it was copied in full, or ask your Plato admin for a new one.Copy the key again in full, or make a new one (Step 1).
We could not find this Plato account. Check the account name, or ask your Plato admin for it.Check the account name with Plato support.
This Plato account has no API access. Ask Plato support to turn it on.Ask Plato support to turn on API access, then press Test the connection again.
Plato did not answer. Try again in a few minutes.Wait a few minutes, then press Test the connection again.
Plato did not accept the request. Try again in a few minutes, or tell us so we can check it.Try again. If it repeats, reply to your 41 Labs contact.

At Step 5, under Name the calendars:

Plato sent no calendars. Check that your Plato account has at least one calendar, then test again.Add a calendar in Plato, press Back, then press Test again.

At Steps 6 to 8, a red line under the week. Next: choose who books stays off until you fix it:

<Day> closes before it opens. Set a closing time after <time>.Set a closing time after the opening time for that day.
Set both an opening and a closing time for <Day>.Fill both time boxes for that day, or switch the day off.
The last start on <Day> must be after <open> and before <close>.Set a last start inside that day's hours, or clear it.
The lunch break on <Day> must be inside <open> to <close>, with the end after the start.Set a lunch break inside that day's hours, or switch it off.
You can list up to 60 closed dates.Remove a date before you add another.

At Step 11, a red banner above the buttons. Nothing was saved, and the form keeps your entries:

Could not save the Plato key. Try again in a minute.Wait a minute, then press Connect Plato again.
Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.Check your internet connection, then press Connect Plato again.
That calendar is not in your Plato. Test the connection again to refresh the list.A calendar changed in Plato during the setup. Press Back to part 1 and press Test again.
A calendar name can have up to 60 characters. Shorten the name for <calendar>.Press Back to part 2 and shorten that name.
Any message from Step 3 or 4The key stopped working between the test and the save. Make a new key (Step 1), then press Connect Plato again.

At Step 13, or after it:

Your AI does not answer your test message.The phone's number is on your alert list. Test from another phone.
Your team heard nothing about a booking.Open your Plato diary and look for appointments with the status Scheduled. Then open Settings → Team & Alerts and press Send test beside each number.

On the Plato page afterwards:

The Needs you pill with: Plato did not accept the key. Make a new key in Plato and connect again.Make a new key in Plato (Step 1), press Connect again, and enter it.
The Needs you pill with: This Plato account has no API access. Ask Plato support to turn it on, then connect again.Ask Plato support, then press Connect again.
The Needs you pill with: Plato could not find this account. Check the account name and connect again.Press Connect again and check the account name.
The Needs you pill with: Plato did not answer several times in a row. Your AI hands bookings to your team until it answers again.Nothing to do. The pill goes back to Working when Plato answers again.
The Needs you pill with: We could not read the stored Plato key. Connect Plato again. Or: No Plato key is stored. Connect Plato again.Press Connect again and enter the key.
Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.Check your internet connection and try again. A switch goes back to where it was.
Plato is not connected. Connect it first.Go to Settings → Connections and connect Plato from Step 2.
